_purpose: The PropEvolve equivalent of the shipped algoTraderAI strategy: a reasoning policy that learns the Expansion + order-flow setup, with the RL stage teaching the prop-challenge constraints. The comparison target is production measured on four unseen eval seeds at 250 episodes: 55.0% pass, 35.5% win rate, 4.15R average winner, +0.83R expectancy, zero blow.
_ticker_note: NQ only. Order flow exists for no other market in this program, and the setup is defined by it.
_split_note: Redrawn. PropEvolve's stock split validates on 2025, which is development data for the Expansion + flow rule and for every algoTraderAI measurement, so reusing it would report a number that has already been optimised against. Training stops at 2024-01-01 and validation covers 2024, leaving 2025 untouched here as the honest comparison window against the shipped PPO. 2026 remains sealed.
_anchor_note: Anchors are PropEvolve's own economic barrier labels — each bar keeps the action its forward outcome justifies, so the policy learns which entries are profitable and which lose — but the candidate ROWS are restricted to the Expansion + order-flow setup. Same labels, same machinery, same error-selected distillation; only the study population changes, to the setups algoTraderAI actually trades.

setup_signals._gate_note: gate_entries ON. The v2 run measured the policy direction at 0.4905 balanced accuracy over 4000 iterations while management reached 0.9248, so the side is handed to the frozen flow rule (sign(persistence_45), +$300,556 net 2021-2025) and the policy is measured on what it demonstrably learns: selection and management. This is an ENVIRONMENT gate — it changes rollouts and evaluation, not the economic SFT labels, which stay forward-outcome based.

_setup_row_filter_note: trigger. Measured on the armed dataset: the rule fires on only ~12% of armed bars, so 88% of directional rows carried NO rule side and the economic label there is an oracle nobody can predict. That put the direction ceiling at 0.504 (train) / 0.509 (valid) and the v2 policy scored 0.4905 — at the ceiling. The armed window did not let the policy learn to disagree with the rule; it drowned the 12% learnable rows in noise. On triggered bars the rule side is correct 0.529 (train) / 0.572 (valid), which is learnable, and WAIT-vs-ENTER there becomes the real question: the rule fired, is this setup worth taking?
_sampling_note: Triggered rows are scarce: train has 3860 across the three actions (WAIT 1328 / LONG 1304 / SHORT 1228) against 31444 armed, so 3000 per action is impossible under setup_row_filter=trigger. 1200/400 fits inside the smallest class with margin. The dataset is ~4x smaller than the armed one, which is the deliberate trade: every row now carries a rule side instead of 88 percent of them carrying none.
_risk_override_note: algoTraderAI Stage A zero-blow foundation: $750 soft daily loss and a K=2 / 65-bar loss-streak cooldown. Applied as a job override so source_environment.json and therefore source_identity stay untouched and the trigger dataset lineage holds. Measured on the rule alone these take blow 46.2% -> ~14%; the remaining safety and all the lost pass rate is what the RL stage has to learn.
